transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because my body just feels completely drained. It's... it's like even just walking from my car into the clinic today, or, you know, being at work and just opening up the EHR... it just takes everything I have. I don't have any energy left.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah, I have. After all that energy I had just dropped off, I started feeling really empty. Just... hopeless most days. It feels like I've already ruined my future in healthcare before it even really started.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I don't think so. I mean, I still want to do stuff. Like, I still like playing games or... watching movies. It's not that I don't care about them anymore. I just don't have the physical energy to actually sit up and do them right now. But the interest is still there, I'm pretty sure.
After you push yourself physically or mentally, do you usually feel much worse afterward?

Not really, no. I mean, I don't think I feel worse afterward. It's more just... I'm already so drained before I even try to do anything. Pushing myself is really hard, but once I stop, I just go back to feeling the exact same amount of tired. I haven't really noticed a big crash or anything like that.
Have you been worrying a lot about different things lately?

No, not really. I mean, I feel pretty bad about messing up my job, like I said, but I wouldn't call it worrying about a bunch of different things. I'm not really anxious or anything like that. Honestly, my brain just feels too... slow and tired to really worry right now. I just kind of lay there.
Did these symptoms start after a specific stressful event?
Yeah, I think so. Um, the clinic where I work changed my responsibilities a while back. The whole crisis just kind of built up over about two months after they did that.
For most of the day, do you feel depressed or hopeless?

Yeah, pretty much. After all that energy I had just dropped, I started feeling really empty most of the time. Just... hopeless. It's like I sit there thinking I've already ruined my future in healthcare, and I'm only 18, so it barely even started. But yeah, most of the day, I just feel really down.
Have you noticed your appetite has changed?

Yeah, definitely. I barely wanted food for a while. I would just skip lunch and dinner completely. I didn't even notice until I realized my scrubs were hanging looser on me. I think I was mostly just drinking coffee or water instead of actually eating.
How has your sleep been lately?

Well, it's been all over the place. Um, for a while there, I could sleep only two or three hours a night and still feel totally wired. But lately... it's different. Now I either wake up way before dawn, just feeling sick with worry, or I end up sleeping half the day and still feel completely exhausted.
During that time when you were sleeping only two or three hours a night and still felt wired, did you also feel unusually energized or euphoric?

Yeah, I did. Um, some days I just felt amazing, like I was completely unstoppable. But it wasn't just feeling good. If someone at work corrected my documentation or told me I needed to slow down, I would just snap at them. It felt like they were insulting me, and I would get really irritable really fast.
During that time, were you more active than usual or taking on a lot more tasks than normal?

Yeah, I was. I just... I had so much energy I couldn't sit still. I would just keep walking the halls at work, reorganizing all the supply closets, checking on rooms. I was constantly looking for more things to do, even when my shift was supposed to be over. I just kept going.
During that time when you felt unstoppable, did you feel unusually confident or powerful, like you could do things other people couldn't?

Yeah, I did. I mean, I really believed I understood patient care better than the actual nurses and the managers. It made total sense to me at the time. I thought that if they would just listen to my ideas, I could completely change the whole system. I felt like I was the only one who really knew how things should be run.
About how many days in a row did that period of feeling wired and unstoppable last?
I'm honestly not sure. Um... when you're only sleeping a couple hours a night, the days just kind of run into each other. I didn't really keep track of exactly how many days it lasted.
During that wired, unstoppable period, did it cause serious problems at work or lead anyone to think you needed emergency psychiatric care or hospitalization?

Yeah, it definitely caused problems. I mean, I got to the point where I couldn't even finish my documentation safely. I just couldn't stay focused on the actual patient-support tasks I was supposed to be doing. It got so bad that employee health actually pulled me from work and sent me straight for an emergency evaluation. And... I also had to stop studying for my CNA certification because I just couldn't keep up with it anymore.
